issue: Systematic skill/difficulty mislabel: every item from far-gov-21 to far-gov-31 is labeled skill 'analysis' and difficulty 3, but each is a one-fact recall or a one-step application. Several are pure recall labeled analysis (two levels off), and far-gov-26 is also flagged calc:true with no computation.
evidence: All 10 'analysis' labels in the module sit on items 21-31, and each of those items is difficulty 3. Recall items labeled analysis: far-gov-22 (compensated absences recognized when due), far-gov-27 (bond proceeds = other financing source; the near-identical far-gov-16 is labeled application/2), far-gov-31 (DB plan assets -> pension trust fund), far-gov-26 (capital outlay = GF expenditure / government-wide asset; far-gov-03 and -12 test the same facts at application/2) and far-gov-28 (principal repayment reduces the liability government-wide). One-step application items labeled analysis: far-gov-21 (sign of one reconciling item), far-gov-24 (900,000 + 40,000; the harder exam twin far-x1-17 with uncollectibles is application/2), far-gov-25 (500,000 - 300,000 - 50,000), far-gov-29 (60,000 / 5) and far-gov-30 (5,000,000 - 3,000,000; the identical far-gov-23 is application/2). No item examines interrelationships or draws conclusions from several data sources, which is what the Blueprint means by Analysis. The labels also inflate the module's analysis share (10 of 31 practice items) and make the easy-to-hard progression artificial.
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill-level definitions (Remembering & Understanding / Application / Analysis)
fix: Relabel: far-gov-21 application/2; -22 remembering/2; -24 application/2; -25 application/2; -26 application/1 with calc:false; -27 remembering/1 (or delete it as a duplicate of -16); -28 application/2; -29 application/2; -30 application/2 (or delete it as a duplicate of -23); -31 remembering/1.

issue: Seven practice MCQs test government mechanics that the 2024+ Blueprints place in BAR Area III. They cover budgetary entries, encumbrances, interfund transfers, fund-to-government-wide reconciliation and compensated-absence liabilities. None is marked optional, and the lesson never teaches any of them, so they count toward FAR readiness while drilling untaught, off-Blueprint content.
evidence: Reference sheets: blueprint-notes FAR I.C says state and local government is 'foundational only: the ACFR, measurement focus, basis of accounting, fund types and net position. Full government accounting is BAR Area III.' far-standards §1c lists for BAR 'deriving government-wide statements and the reconciliations, specific transactions (capital assets, long-term liabilities, interfund activity, nonexchange revenue, budgetary and encumbrance entries)'. SuperFastCPA files the reconciliation and fund-balance computations as BAR tasks ('BAR CPA Exam: How to prepare a schedule to reconcile fund balances ... to net position in government-wide statements'; 'BAR CPA Exam: How to Calculate the Fund Balances ... and Prepare Journal Entries'). Lesson check: it never mentions budgets, appropriations, encumbrances, transfers or compensated absences, and for the reconciliation it says only 'a reconciliation between the two is required' (worked insight), with no adjustments taught. far-gov-18, for example, needs + capital outlay - depreciation - bond proceeds + principal repaid (-100,000 + 2,000,000 - 600,000 - 3,000,000 + 500,000 = -1,200,000). That is 7 of 31 practice items (23%).
source: AICPA 2026 FAR/BAR Blueprints (FAR I.C vs BAR III), per review/reference/blueprint-notes.md and far-standards.md §1c; https://www.superfastcpa.com/bar-cpa-exam-how-to-prepare-a-schedule-to-reconcile-fund-balances-in-the-governmental-financial-statements-to-net-position-in-government-wide-statements/
fix: Mark far-gov-13, -15, -18, -20, -21, -22 and -25 optional:true, as REVIEW.md P2-2 did for the other off-Blueprint items, or move them to BAR content. Backfill with in-scope FAR items (for example: statement of activities net (expense) revenue and program vs. general revenues; what the government-wide statements include and exclude; deferred inflows of resources; proprietary vs. fiduciary statement names). If any item is kept as core, add the matching lesson section.

issue: Lesson-item alignment gap for in-scope content. The lesson names the fund types only in a diagram and never says what special revenue, debt service, capital projects, custodial or investment trust funds are for. Items and all three TBS ask the learner to classify activities into exactly those funds. RSI contents and the treatment of debt principal are also tested but not taught.
evidence: The mermaid diagram (lines 57-73) gives a purpose only for enterprise, internal service, permanent and private-purpose trust funds. Items that need the missing definitions: far-gov-02; far-tbs-r3-property-tax rows a2-a4 (capital projects, special revenue, debt service); far-tbs-u4-government-plans rows c, d, e (special revenue, debt service, custodial for taxes collected for a school district); far-tbs-x1-government rows f1, f2, f5, f7. far-gov-17 asks which items are RSI, but the lesson lists RSI only as a component of the ACFR (MD&A is listed separately and nothing says it is RSI). far-gov-19 and -28 need 'principal repayment is an expenditure in the fund and reduces the liability government-wide'. The lesson says only 'debt service recognized when due'.
source: GASB 54 ¶¶29-35 (governmental fund type definitions); GASB 84 (custodial funds); GASB 34 ¶8 as amended by GASB 103 (MD&A and RSI)
fix: Add a 'What each fund is for' table with one line and one example per fund type. Use GASB 54 wording for special revenue (restricted or committed revenue sources that make up a substantial portion of inflows), capital projects, debt service and permanent funds, plus custodial vs. trust funds. Add one sentence that MD&A and budgetary comparison schedules are RSI, and one that debt principal paid is a fund expenditure but reduces bonds payable government-wide.

issue: The net investment in capital assets definition ('capital assets, net of depreciation, minus related debt') omits the unspent-proceeds rule. In the lesson's own worked example the rule gives a wrong figure.
evidence: Worked example: $2,000,000 of bonds, $1,500,000 spent on a fire station, $500,000 unspent at December 31. Applying the lesson's rule: 1,500,000 - 2,000,000 = -500,000 NICA. Under GASB 63 ¶9 (Cod. 2200.118), the portion of debt attributable to unspent proceeds is excluded from NICA and goes into the same component as the unspent proceeds (here restricted). So NICA = 1,500,000 - 1,500,000 = 0, and the remaining 500,000 debt offsets the 500,000 restricted cash. Deferred outflows and inflows attributable to capital debt are also part of the definition.
fix: Amend line 87: 'capital assets net of accumulated depreciation, minus the outstanding debt (and related deferred outflows/inflows) attributable to acquiring or building them; debt proceeds not yet spent are excluded.' Optionally add a step to the worked example showing NICA = 0 and restricted net position = 0 (500,000 cash - 500,000 related debt).

issue: Duplicate and near-duplicate practice items: five items repeat another item's fact in the same way, taking slots from untested in-scope topics.
evidence: far-gov-11 has the same stem as far-gov-01 (automated Jaccard 1.00) with the same answer content; only the letter moves. far-gov-27 is far-gov-16 again: $5,000,000 bond proceeds received by a capital projects fund -> other financing source. The same fact is also in far-gov-pre1, far-gov-fc7 and the lesson big idea. far-gov-30 is far-gov-23 with different numbers (net capital assets - related debt). far-gov-14 is far-gov-04 (inventory -> nonspendable). far-gov-26 merges far-gov-03 (truck = fund expenditure) and far-gov-12 (truck capitalized government-wide). Meanwhile no item covers program vs. general revenues, the statement of activities format, major funds, component units, deferred outflows/inflows, or proprietary and fiduciary statement names.
fix: Delete far-gov-11, -27 and -30, and replace -14 and -26 with new in-scope items. Suggested topics: net (expense) revenue by function and program revenues (charges for services, operating/capital grants) vs. general revenues (taxes); what government-wide statements exclude (fiduciary) and how internal service funds fold into governmental activities; deferred inflows of resources; the names of proprietary and fiduciary fund statements.

issue: Practice items reappear almost verbatim on mock exams, and mock 3 tests the 60-day property tax rule three times. A learner who did the practice set sees recognition items on the mock, and one mock item cues another.
evidence: far-gov-24 (practice): $1,000,000 levy, $900,000 collected, $40,000 within 60 days -> $940,000. far-x1-17 (exam, on far-mock-1 and far-mock-3) has the same $1,000,000 / $900,000 / $40,000 and the same $940,000 key. far-tbs-r3-property-tax (practice) and far-tbs-x1-government (exam, on far-mock-3) share a $5,000,000 levy, 2% uncollectible and the same fund-classification rows: utility -> enterprise, bond proceeds -> capital projects, gas tax -> special revenue, GO debt -> debt service, motor pool -> internal service, park endowment -> permanent. far-mock-3 contains far-x1-17, far-x1-35 and the TBS pt part, all testing 60-day availability, and the far-x1-17 stem ('expects to collect $40,000 within 60 days after year-end') cues the answer to far-x1-35.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 6 (one item revealing another) and 7 (duplicates); content/far/exams/far-mock-1.json, far-mock-3.json
fix: Change the figures in far-gov-24 (for example a $2,400,000 levy) and change the activities and levy in far-tbs-r3-property-tax (for example a special assessment, an airport, an investment pool). On far-mock-3, replace far-x1-35 or far-x1-17 with an in-scope item on a different concept (for example fiduciary exclusion or net position components).

issue: The availability rule is worded loosely as 'collected within (about) 60 days'. It leaves out 'during the year or' and/or 'after year-end', so read literally the keyed option excludes taxes collected earlier in the year.
evidence: far-x1-35 key (a): 'Levied for 2025 and collected within 60 days'. Within 60 days of what? Read literally, a 2025 tax collected in March 2025 does not qualify, yet it is revenue. far-gov-07 key (c): '(collected within about 60 days)'. far-gov-fc6 back: 'collected within ~60 days after year-end' omits collections during the year. far-gov-24 choice (a) rationale: 'Revenue is collected within 60 days.' By contrast, the glossary ('Available (modified accrual)': 'Collected within the period or soon enough afterward (generally 60 days...)') and the lesson (line 53) state the rule correctly. Under GASB Cod. P70, available means collected within the current period or expected to be collected soon enough thereafter to pay current liabilities, not to exceed 60 days.
source: NCGA Interpretation 3 / GASB Codification P70.104; GASB 33
fix: Reword far-x1-35 (a) to 'Levied for 2025 and collected during 2025 or within 60 days after year-end', and far-gov-07 (c) to 'When measurable and available (collected during the year or within 60 days after year-end)'. Make fc6 read '...collected during the year or within 60 days after year-end'. Make far-gov-24 (a) read 'Correct. 900,000 collected during the year + 40,000 collected within 60 days after year-end.'

issue: The exam TBS never states the availability period. The pt answers (revenue 4,700,000, deferred inflows 200,000) work only if the learner assumes a 60-day period, while the practice twin far-tbs-r3-property-tax states it.
evidence: Exhibit: collected 4,500,000 in 2025; 200,000 collected January 1 - February 28, 2026; 200,000 later in 2026. Key: rev = 4,500,000 + 200,000 = 4,700,000 and def = 4,900,000 - 4,700,000 = 200,000 (recomputed: 5,000,000 × 98% = 4,900,000). Both rows assume collections through February 28 (59 days) are 'available'. GASB sets 60 days as a ceiling ('not to exceed 60 days'), and each government discloses its own period. With a 30-day policy, for example, the answer changes.
source: GASB Codification P70.104 (property taxes: available = collected within 60 days after year-end, not to exceed)
fix: Add '(the city uses a 60-day availability period for property taxes)' to the instructions or the exhibit.

issue: Distractor rationales are thin or circular ('Not the computation.', 'Not the treatment.'), and several trap labels don't match the misconception the distractor models.
evidence: far-gov-24 (d) $960,000, far-gov-25 (d) $250,000, far-gov-29 (d) $6,000 and far-gov-30 (d) $8,000,000 each say only 'Not the computation.' far-gov-27 (c) says 'Not the treatment.' Recomputed misconceptions: 25(d) 250,000 = 500,000 - 300,000 + 50,000 (encumbrance added: wrong-sign, labeled distractor-number). 30(d) 8,000,000 = 5,000,000 + 3,000,000 (wrong-sign; its twin 23(d) is labeled wrong-sign). 29(d) 6,000 = a half-year convention on 12,000, which the stem's 'first full year' rules out. 24(d) 960,000 = 1,000,000 - 40,000, an unexplained reversal. Trap mismatches: far-gov-12 (b) 'Reported only in the general fund' is labeled 'reversed', but it is a fund-vs-government-wide classification error. far-gov-26 (d) is labeled 'partial-computation' in a no-computation item. far-gov-12 (a) rationale 'Expensing applies in the fund statements as an expenditure' blurs expense and expenditure. far-gov-21 (d) 'Report it as revenue' is not a reconciliation action, so it is implausible.
fix: Write rationales that name the error. For example 25(d): 'Adds the 50,000 of encumbrances instead of subtracting them' (trap wrong-sign). 30(d): 'Adds the related debt to the assets' (wrong-sign). 29(d): 'Takes a half-year of depreciation; the stem asks for a full year' (wrong-period). 24(d): 'Subtracts the 60-day collections from the levy instead of adding them to collections' (other). 27(c): 'Deferred inflows are resources applicable to future periods, e.g., taxes not yet available; bond proceeds are a financing source.' Relabel 12(b) wrong-classification and 26(d) wrong-classification. Replace 21(d) with 'Add it only if the bonds are used for capital assets'. Reword 12(a) as 'In the fund the truck is an expenditure, not an expense; government-wide it is capitalized.'

issue: These calculation items' explanations state the rule but not the computation, and far-gov-29's stem omits the depreciation method and salvage value the key depends on.
evidence: far-gov-24 explanation: 'property tax revenue includes collections within 60 days of year-end'. It shows neither 900,000 + 40,000 = 940,000 nor the 60,000 deferred inflow. far-gov-29 explanation: 'Proprietary funds use the economic resources measurement focus and record depreciation'. The 12,000 key requires straight-line with zero salvage (60,000 / 5), and the stem states neither.
fix: far-gov-24: append '900,000 + 40,000 = 940,000; the remaining 60,000 is a deferred inflow of resources.' far-gov-29: add 'straight-line, no salvage value' to the stem and '60,000 ÷ 5 = 12,000 depreciation expense; no expenditure, because enterprise funds use full accrual' to the explanation.

issue: Answer cues and overlapping options: in each of these items an option structure or wording gives away the key.
evidence: far-gov-05: the stem asks for a component of net position, which rules out (d) 'Nonspendable fund balance' on its face. The key also repeats the stem's 'capital assets', and the item explanation just lists the three components. far-gov-10: (a) 'They are reported in the government-wide statement of net position' and (c) 'They're excluded from government-wide statements' are logical opposites, so one must be the key. far-gov-13: key (a) 'Within fund balance' contains distractor (c) 'As nonspendable fund balance', so the options overlap. far-gov-16: every distractor begins 'As ...' and the key 'Other financing source' does not, which breaks parallelism.
fix: far-gov-05: replace (d) with a plausible net position distractor such as 'Restricted for capital projects' or 'Committed for capital outlay'. far-gov-10: replace (a) or (c) so they are not complementary, for example (a) 'They are reported in a separate column of the government-wide statements', with the key unchanged. far-gov-13: make the key specific ('Included in restricted, committed or assigned fund balance as appropriate; not liabilities') so it no longer subsumes (c). far-gov-16: make the key 'As an other financing source'.

issue: Neither the lesson nor far-gov-17 mentions GASB 103 (Financial Reporting Model Improvements), which applies to fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2025 and is testable throughout 2026. It changes several 'format and content' points that sit in FAR's foundational scope.
evidence: The lesson citations list GASB 34, 54 and 84 and Cod. 1100/1300/2200, with no GASB 103. far-gov-17's explanation cites 'GASB 34: MD&A and budgetary comparison schedules (among others) are RSI'. Under GASB 34 the budgetary comparison could instead be presented as a basic statement. GASB 103 makes it RSI only, requires variance columns, sets five MD&A sections, replaces extraordinary and special items with separately presented unusual or infrequent items, and adds the proprietary-fund subtotal 'operating income (loss) and noncapital subsidies'. The keys are still correct.
source: GASB Statement 103 (issued 2024; FY beginning after 6/15/2025), per review/reference/far-standards.md §4b and 'GASB 103 in detail'
fix: Add GASB 103 to the lesson citations and a short ACFR note: MD&A (five required sections) and the budgetary comparison for the general fund and major special revenue funds are RSI. Cite 'GASB 34 as amended by GASB 103' in far-gov-17.

issue: The GASB 54 fund balance table is slightly incomplete. 'Assigned' omits intent expressed by the governing body itself and omits the rule that positive residuals in other governmental funds are assigned. 'Committed' omits that the constraint is removed only by the same type of action.
evidence: Lesson line 98: 'Assigned — Intended use set by a body or official delegated authority'. GASB 54 ¶13-14: intent may be expressed by (a) the governing body itself or (b) a body or official to which it delegated authority, and in governmental funds other than the general fund, all positive remaining amounts are assigned. far-gov-chk2 (c) rationale repeats the narrow version ('intent by a delegated body or official'). Line 97, Committed, omits 'can be changed only by the same type of formal action', which chk2's stem relies on.
fix: Assigned: 'Intended use set by the governing body or by a body or official it has delegated; also all positive residual fund balance in governmental funds other than the general fund.' Committed: add 'removed or changed only by the same formal action'.

issue: Realism: a city sponsoring a '401(k)-type' plan. State and local governments generally cannot establish 401(k) plans, and their DC plans are 457(b) or 401(a) plans. The part prompt also refers to 'Year 2' with no year context in the exhibit.
evidence: IRC §401(k)(4)(B)(ii) bars state and local governments from sponsoring cash or deferred arrangements (pre-May 6, 1986 plans are grandfathered). The exhibit title reads 'Employee 401(k)-type plan data', and the plan part says 'Compute for the plan's Year 2 statement'. Numbers recomputed: additions 780,000 + 390,000 + 150,000 + 520,000 = 1,840,000; deductions 610,000 + 25,000 = 635,000; ending 6,400,000 + 1,840,000 − 635,000 = 7,605,000. All keys correct.
source: IRC §401(k)(4)(B)(ii); GASB 84 ¶¶11-12 and GASB 97 (DC plans as fiduciary activities)
fix: Rename the exhibit 'Employee 457(b) deferred compensation plan data' (or '401(a) defined contribution plan') and change 'Year 2' to 'the current year'.

issue: The levy exhibit's phrase 'the rest is expected later' is loose next to the 2% uncollectible allowance. The dropdown rows are labeled only '1' to '6', which forces the learner to flip back to the exhibit.
evidence: 5,000,000 − 4,600,000 − 150,000 = 250,000 uncollected. Of that, 100,000 (2%) is uncollectible and 150,000 is expected later, which gives the keyed defi = 150,000 and gw = 4,900,000. A literal reading of 'the rest' (250,000) gives defi 250,000, and with tolerance 0 that is scored wrong. The sister TBS far-tbs-x1-government states 'Remaining collectible amount expected later: $200,000' explicitly.
fix: Exhibit: 'the remaining collectible amount ($150,000) is expected later in the following year.' Give the dropdown rows descriptive labels (for example '1 — Water utility billing residents').
